places.name: Psiri (Psyrri)
places.background: A former craftsmen's quarter next to Monastiraki, now packed with tavernas, bars, street art and late-night music. It is fairly alternative and gritty-bohemian (but busy with visitors), with no poshness at all.

photos.credit: Photo: Badseed · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons
Photo: Pavlos1988 · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

places.name: Monastiraki
places.background: The busy square, metro hub and flea market below the Acropolis, full of souvenir and vintage stalls and rooftop bars with views. Lively and mainstream-touristy, with a slightly scruffy edge. Not posh.

photos.credit: Photo: C messier · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons
Photo: Antonio Fajardo López · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons
Photo: Badseed · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons
Photo: George E. Koronaios · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

places.name: Ta Karamanlidika tou Fani
places.background: A deli and charcuterie shop with a busy meze restaurant attached, serving pastirma, soutzouki, cured meats, cheeses and Anatolian-Greek small plates with ouzo, tsipouro and wine. It is built on the cured-meat traditions of the Karamanlides, Anatolian Greek-Orthodox refugees. Fanis Theodoropoulos continues his family's 1920s pastirma trade, and the restaurant has occupied its corner neoclassical building since 2014.
places.address: Sokratous 1 & Evripidou, Athens 105 52 (deli/pastirma shop at Evripidou 41)

places.name: Linou Soumpasis & Sia (LS & SIA)
places.background: A hyped modern-Greek neo-taverna and bistro in a former candle shop in Psyrri. It is dinner-focused with a natural-wine list and no cocktail menu, reservations needed, Michelin Plate 2024-2025. Opened in December 2021 by Myrsini Linou and George Soumpasis, it is also a shop, natural-candle maker and creative office, and hosts exhibitions and record launches.

places.name: Cafe Avissinia
places.background: An old-school taverna and mezedopoleio on the Monastiraki flea-market square, mainly a sit-down meal place, on three levels with an Acropolis-view rooftop terrace. There is live folk music (accordion, piano) at weekends from September to June. Ketty Koufonikola opened it in 1986, and the interior is cluttered with antiques.

places.name: Wine is Fine
places.background: A French-bistro-style natural-wine bar that works as a small restaurant, with a full seasonal menu of French-Greek small plates and white tablecloths on pedestrian Vissis St. It is walk-in only with a long waitlist. Two Frenchmen, Rafael Wallon-Brownstone and Thomas Brengou, run it with Greek chef Stavros Chrysafidis, in a 70s-chic interior.

places.name: Booze Cooperativa (K.O.T.E.S.)
places.background: A multi-level arty bar and cultural space with galleries and a performance basement, open from late morning. By day people come for coffee, chess and backgammon, and at night it turns into a loud bar with indoor smoking. Founded in 1989 in a neoclassical building, it has also been the headquarters of K.O.T.E.S., a tongue-in-cheek smokers' party, since 2018.

places.name: Cantina Social
places.background: An unsigned courtyard and garden bar at the end of an alley off Leokoriou in Psyrri/Thiseio. It is a café by day and a dance bar at night with resident DJs (techno, indie, disco), cheap drinks and late hours. It is set in an old lodge and is a locals' hangout.

places.name: Couleur Locale
places.background: An all-day rooftop bar and bistro in a Monastiraki arcade by the flea market, with a direct Acropolis view. Coffee and brunch by day, then a cocktail bar with DJs and jazz, soul and rock at night, plus light food. It opened in 2014 on the top floor of a shabby-looking building.

places.name: TAF - The Art Foundation
places.background: A courtyard café-bar in an art complex with galleries and a shop, in 1870s residential buildings around a tree-filled courtyard. Coffee by day, beers and simple cocktails at night, with an arty young crowd and underground music. It has run since about 2014.

places.name: Retiré (at Ergon House)
places.background: A seasonal (April to October) third-floor rooftop bar on the Ergon House food hall and hotel, with Acropolis views. Cocktails by The Clumsies come from a cocktail truck, with Greek wines, beers and light bites. Casual and walk-in only.
places.address: Mitropoleos 23 (3rd-floor terrace of Ergon House), Athens 105 57

places.name: Hyper Hypo
places.background: Independent bookstore for art, design, photography, architecture, fashion and pop culture, with a project space for talks, launches and exhibitions; also sells posters and prints.

photos.credit: Photo: hyperhypo.gr

places.name: Plaka
places.background: The oldest quarter, right under the Acropolis: pedestrian lanes, neoclassical houses and the Cycladic-style Anafiotika hamlet. Pretty and very touristy, neither alternative nor posh (tourist-priced tavernas).

photos.credit: Photo: Glorious 93 · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons
Photo: C messier · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons
Photo: C messier · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons
Photo: Giorgoos · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

places.name: Dopios
places.background: A modern Greek meze restaurant by chef Christoforos Peskias, a sit-down dinner place with a solid cocktail and wine list. It focuses on small producers from around Greece. It has run since about 2021 under plane trees on Agion Theodoron square, beside the 11th-century church of Agioi Theodoroi.

photos.credit: Photo: dopiosrestaurant.gr

places.name: The Clumsies
places.background: A cocktail bar in a townhouse, open all day across several floors but mainly a cocktail destination, with a small food menu. Vassilis Kyritsis and Nikos Bakoulis founded it in 2014. It has been on the World's 50 Best Bars list every year since 2015, peaking at No. 3 in 2020.

places.name: Baba Au Rum
places.background: A rum-focused cocktail bar in Psyrri with 400+ rums and tropical, retro decor. No reservations. Open for over 15 years, it is a regular on the World's 50 Best Bars list (No. 27 in 2025).

places.name: Blue Bird
places.background: A tiny (about 23 m²) cocktail bar on pedestrian Ipitou street near Syntagma, open evenings and nights. At weekends it spills onto the street and square with resident DJs and a street-party crowd. It calls itself a 'bar for exotic birds' and started out serving only spirits.

places.name: Dybbuk
places.background: A large electronic dance club with house and techno nights, known for big production nights and winter-only seasons. Its last known home was the Stadiou 7 arcade near Syntagma, its third location. It opened around 2009 in a Kolonaki basement at Patriarchou Ioakeim 37.

places.name: Seychelles
places.background: Seychelles (Σεϋχέλλες) is a modern-Greek sharing-plates restaurant with outdoor tables on a lively pedestrian square in Metaxourgeio/Kerameikos. Booking is recommended. An early Athens 'bistronomy' spot, it serves ingredient-driven Greek 'soul food' with rustic-meets-urban cooking and is popular with locals and tourists.

places.name: Beauty Killed the Beast
places.background: An all-day café-bar on the pedestrian part of Paramythias in Kerameikos: coffee and brunch by day, DJs and cocktails at night, with a garden. It is in a restored 1930s neoclassical mansion with King Kong art on the facade.

places.name: SMUT Athens
places.background: An underground queer techno club at Vatsaxi 4, in an industrial space in Metaxourgeio, open on Saturday nights. There is a no-camera policy and a consent briefing at the door, as part of its safe-space approach. The look is raw, red-lit Berlin warehouse.

places.name: Sodade2
places.background: A long-running LGBTQ+ dance club in Gazi with two dance floors, one for mainstream and Greek pop, one for house and progressive. It is weekend-focused, late and packed with a younger crowd. One of the first gay clubs in Gazi and still one of the most popular.

places.name: S-Cape
places.background: A large, long-running two-level LGBTQ+ dance club in Gazi with pop and Greek music, drag shows, go-go dancers and themed nights. It has several bars and stages, cheap drinks and a young crowd.

places.name: Alekos Fassianos Museum
places.background: The painter Alekos Fassianos's family home, an apartment block he remodelled with architect Kyriakos Krokos over two decades (finished 1996); opened as a museum to his work in 2023.

places.name: Benaki Museum - Pireos 138
places.background: The Benaki's large contemporary venue in a converted industrial building, used for temporary exhibitions of art, architecture and photography.

places.name: The Breeder
places.background: Leading contemporary art gallery founded in 2002 by Stathis Panagoulis and George Vamvakidis, growing out of The Breeder magazine. It is in a converted 1970s ice-cream factory and shows Greek and international artists at major fairs.

places.name: To Rini
places.background: A tiny chef-run all-day bistro by the National Archaeological Museum, with a quiet patio. Coffee and brunch from the morning, then modern takes on Greek comfort dishes from seasonal produce, with natural Greek wines, in the evening.

places.name: Pharaoh
places.background: A lively wood-fire Greek restaurant and natural-wine bar (Michelin Bib Gourmand) with a vinyl DJ in the evenings, turning party-ish late at night. Chef Manolis Papoutsakis cooks without electricity, using wood stoves, charcoal and a wood oven. It sits behind a heavy curtain in edgy Exarchia.

places.name: I Kriti (Η Κρήτη)
places.background: A family-run Cretan taverna and rakadiko in an arcade (stoa) off Veranzerou, by Kaningos Sq. It serves home-style Cretan dishes such as apaki, Sfakian pies and liver with honey, with raki and a free dessert, using produce from Cretan cooperatives. Running for about 30 years, it is now seen as a classic.

places.name: Ouzeri Lesvos
places.background: An unpretentious, old-fashioned Exarchia ouzeri serving fresh seafood and meze from Lesvos or cooked the Lesvos way, at modest prices. It is long-standing, crowded and mostly local.

places.name: Zigoala (Ζιγκοάλα)
places.background: A modern taverna (mageirio) in Omonia by chef Vasilis Chammam, serving meze with Greek and Eastern Mediterranean cooking to laïko music. It was the hyped opening of the 2025-26 season, widely reviewed (Athinorama, Lifo, FNL) and credited with drawing food lovers to Omonia.

places.name: Diporto
places.background: An unmarked basement taverna under an old neoclassical building by the Central Market, lunch only, with shared tables and cash payment. There is no menu: a few daily dishes such as legumes or chickpeas, stews, small fried fish and salad, with retsina from the barrel. It has run since 1887.

places.name: Don't be a D!ck
places.background: An Exarchia 'soft clubbing' bar opened in autumn 2025, with 48-hour sourdough pizza from a wood-fired oven and clean cocktails early, then DJ sets (italo and space disco, funk). Downstairs is the pink-tiled 'Toilet Room' with a disco ball and a no-photo policy. The look is 70s-80s Fiorucci.

places.name: Skullbar
places.background: An underground bar that is an alternative coffee bar by day and a dance club by night. It is best known for weekend after-hours techno and house parties starting around 05:00.

places.name: National Archaeological Museum
places.background: Greece's largest archaeological museum, with prehistoric to late-antique finds: the Mask of Agamemnon, the Artemision Bronze and the Antikythera Mechanism.

photos.credit: Photo: namuseum.gr
Photo: Gary Todd · CC0 · Wikimedia Commons
Photo: Palickap · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons
Photo: Nikos Kitsakis · CC BY 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons
Photo: Thomas Wolf, www.foto-tw.de · CC BY-SA 3.0 de · Wikimedia Commons

places.name: Ninetto Gallery
places.background: Contemporary gallery co-founded by Romain Bitton and Fred de Schonen in a former apartment, so a visit feels like a collector's home; it shows international and Greece-based artists, often their first exhibitions.

places.name: Romantso
places.background: A creative hub in the former printing works of 'Romantso' magazine. It combines a start-up incubator, artist studios and residencies with a café-bar and a busy programme of exhibitions, parties and concerts.

places.name: Kolonaki
places.background: The upscale district on the lower slopes of Lycabettus, with designer boutiques, galleries, embassies and people-watching cafés around Kolonaki Square (Plateia Filikis Etaireias). The poshest neighbourhood in central Athens: establishment and chic, the opposite of alternative.

photos.credit: Photo: Giorgoos · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons
Photo: Giorgoos · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons
Photo: Andrzej Otrębski · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

places.name: Filippou (Taverna Filippou)
places.background: A classic Kolonaki taverna for lunch or dinner, not a bar, with daily-changing home-cooked dishes (mageirefta) from an open kitchen. It is a third-generation family business founded in 1923 as a basement wine shop, at its current ground-floor site since 1968.

places.name: Prasini Tenta
places.background: A café-restaurant on the lower slopes of Lycabettus, by the footpath, with a panoramic city view. Coffee and brunch by day, cocktails and wine at sunset, and a full menu of Greek, Mediterranean and international comfort food. It has operated since 1931.

places.name: Philos Athens
places.background: A daytime brunch café with a concept store (fashion, homeware) and event space across three floors, serving farm-to-table brunch, bowls, eggs, pancakes and coffee. It reportedly will not seat coffee-only customers. The restored 1930s neoclassical townhouse once belonged to collector Evripidis Koutlidis.

places.name: Dexameni (café-ouzeri)
places.background: A historic open-air kafeneio under the trees of Dexameni Square: coffee in the morning, then ouzo or beer with small meze plates through the evening. It is very local. The square is named after Hadrian's 2nd-century reservoir, was a haunt of writers like Papadiamantis and Varnalis, and has a summer open-air cinema (Cine Dexameni).

places.name: Queen Bee
places.background: A Kolonaki bakery-café serving all-day brunch, known for sourdough and croissants (a French baker consulted on them), such as a pistachio-praline one. It is from Panagiotis Kalyvas (of Capanna and Kolonaki Kalamaki) and busy with stylish Kolonaki locals.

places.name: Rock'n'Roll
places.background: A bar-restaurant by day and early evening (burgers, pizza, tacos), then a crowded late party bar with DJs, party nights and live acts. A Kolonaki institution since 1987, with a mixed-age crowd from the smart Kolonaki set.

places.name: Benaki Museum - Nikos Hadjikyriakos-Ghika Gallery
places.background: The former home and studio of modernist painter Nikos Hadjikyriakos-Ghika (1906-94), now a Benaki branch showing his work and that of his circle, with views from the upper floors.

places.name: Benaki Museum (main building)
places.background: The Benaki's flagship mansion, covering Greek art and culture from prehistory to the 20th century; its rooftop café looks over the National Garden.

places.name: Museum of Cycladic Art
places.background: Museum built around the Goulandris collection of Cycladic figurines and ancient Greek and Cypriot art, also staging major contemporary art shows.

places.name: Byzantine & Christian Museum
places.background: A national museum of Byzantine and post-Byzantine art (icons, mosaics, frescoes, manuscripts) in the 1840s Villa Ilissia, built for the Duchess of Plaisance, with a large modern underground extension and gardens.

photos.credit:

places.name: Eleftheria Tseliou Gallery
places.background: Contemporary art gallery founded in 2013 that represents about 15 established and emerging, mostly Greek artists, with around seven solo shows a year.

places.name: Indigo (@indigo_ath)
tips: Giulia: her friend Maya runs it. Tell Maya you're Giulia's friend.
places.background: A small lifestyle and gift boutique (Indigo Atelier) selling handmade jewellery, ceramics and macramé. Co-owned by Niki Protopapa and Maya Simou, which matches Giulia's 'friend Maya'.

places.name: Benaki Museum Shop
places.background: Founded about 40 years ago as the first museum shop in Greece, it sells replicas, jewellery, prints, books and pieces by Greek designers. There are five branches across the Benaki buildings plus an online shop.
places.address: Koumbari 1 & Vas. Sofias Ave, Athens 106 74 (main store; also in other Benaki buildings)

places.name: Lycabettus Hill walk
places.background: At 277 m, the highest hill in central Athens, with the chapel of Agios Georgios on top and 360° views over the city to the sea. You can walk up through pines in about 20-30 minutes, or take the funicular from Aristippou St.
places.address: Lycabettus Hill (paths from Kolonaki, e.g. top of Aristippou / Ploutarchou)

Photo: Gosspil89 · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons
Photo: Gosspil89 · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons
Photo: Dennis David Auger · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

places.name: Pangrati
places.background: A residential district behind the Panathenaic Stadium, centred on Plateia Varnava and Plateia Plastira, with a strong local food and bar scene and few tourists. Middle-class and quietly hip: more neighbourhood-bohemian than either alternative or posh.

photos.credit: Photo: George E. Koronaios · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons
Photo: Tolisr · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons
Photo: Badseed · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons
Photo: Jebulon · CC0 · Wikimedia Commons

places.name: Cookoovaya
places.background: An upscale modern Greek restaurant near Evangelismos, a dinner destination with an open kitchen and a sommelier-led wine list. It opened in 2014 as a collaboration of five Greek chefs, including Periklis Koskinas, and serves generous Mediterranean dishes from small Greek suppliers. It is on Michelin and 50 Best Discovery lists.

places.name: Akra
tips: Recommended by both Irene and Giulia.
places.background: A bistronomy restaurant and bakery with an open kitchen, a counter and a wood-fired grill. It runs as a bakery-café for breakfast, with dinner as the main event. Chefs Giannis Loukakis and Spiros Pediaditakis opened it in 2023, and it holds a Michelin Bib Gourmand (since the 2024 Athens guide).

places.name: Mavro Provato
places.background: A very popular modern mezedopoleio ('black sheep') in Pangrati serving small plates, grills, home-style dishes and tsipouro at fair prices. Reservations recommended. A neighbourhood favourite, with a second branch in Melissia.

places.name: Ohh Boy
places.background: An all-day Pangrati bakery-café and bistro for brunch, porridge, protein pancakes, chia bowls and cakes, with many vegetarian, vegan and gluten-free options. It also serves spritzes, craft beer and wine in the early evening.

places.name: Chelsea Hotel (bar)
places.background: Not a hotel: a bohemian corner café-bar on Plastira Square in a former grocery. Coffee by day, then a busy, cheap neighbourhood bar with craft beer and simple cocktails at night. A Pangrati favourite with young locals.

places.name: Thissio
places.background: The area around the pedestrian Apostolou Pavlou promenade, with cafés facing the Acropolis and the Temple of Hephaestus in the Ancient Agora. Relaxed and somewhat touristy but loved by Athenians for evening strolls: mid-range, neither posh nor very alternative.

photos.credit: Photo: Eusebius · CC BY 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons
Photo: Peter von Hess · CC BY 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons
Photo: Eusebius · CC BY 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons
Photo: Bobby H · CC BY-SA 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

places.name: Filopappou Hill (Philopappos)
tips: Irene: the hill just south of Plaka.
Giulia's walk: cross the hill, then go down west into Petralona and eat at Taverna Oikonomou.
places.background: A pine-covered archaeological hill south-west of the Acropolis, topped by the 2nd-century Philopappos Monument and crossed by Pikionis' stone paths. It has the classic Acropolis and sunset view, is free and open, and has a local, unpretentious feel, more green space than scene.

photos.credit: Photo: Eusebius · CC BY 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons
Photo: giggel · CC BY 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

places.name: Taverna Oikonomou
tips: Giulia's walk: cross Filopappou Hill, go down into Petralona and eat here.
places.background: An old-school Petralona taverna with home-cooked mageirefta (stuffed vegetables, rabbit stifado, beans), courtyard and street tables, and a recited menu. It has operated since the 1930s.

places.name: Phita (Fita / ΦΙΤΑ)
places.background: A modern Greek gastro-taverna in Neos Kosmos, dinner-focused, with a daily-changing, seafood-heavy sharing-plate menu of seafood, vegetables and pulses from small producers, and a curated wine list. Fotis Foteinoglou and Theodoros Kassavetis opened it in 2019, and it is credited with putting Neos Kosmos on the food map.

places.name: Drupes & Drips
places.background: A tiny Koukaki spot with specialty coffee and juices in the morning, then an Italian-style spritz and cicchetti bar. Evenings bring Greek and Italian natural wines, prosecco and raki with cured meats and cheese boards.

places.name: Epta Martyres (Seven Martyrs)
places.background: A Neos Kosmos/Koukaki wine bar with a Volos-tsipouradiko-style kitchen and 150+ Greek and European low-intervention labels, many of them magnums, with 10+ by the glass. Small seafood and meze plates are sent out as you drink, a Volos custom. It opened in 2024 and quickly became a hangout.

places.name: Alcatraz (strip club)
places.warning: Recent TripAdvisor reviews describe tourist scams here (e.g. €950 billed for three drinks, June 2025; hostess drinks charged as €150 bottles; taxi drivers steering people in). Agree prices before ordering, or skip it.
places.background: A strip and 'show club' on Syngrou Avenue, Athens' traditional strip of nightclubs, open 21:00-09:00 with reservations by phone or online. It is repeatedly reported as a tourist trap, with taxi drivers steering customers there and inflated bills.

photos.credit: Photo: alcatrazclub.gr

places.name: Benaki Museum of Islamic Art
places.background: The Benaki's Islamic collection (ceramics, metalwork, textiles, carved woodwork from the 7th-19th c.) in two neoclassical mansions. Part of the ancient city wall is visible in the basement, and there is a rooftop café facing Kerameikos.

places.name: Acropolis Museum
places.background: Bernard Tschumi-designed museum (opened 2009) for finds from the Acropolis, including the Parthenon gallery; glass floors show the excavations below.

photos.credit: Photo: Original uploader was Realfacts at el.wikipedia · Attribution · Wikimedia Commons
Photo: Nikos Kitsakis · CC BY 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons
Photo: Challisrussia · CC0 · Wikimedia Commons
Photo: Martin451 · CC BY 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

places.name: National Observatory of Athens - Thissio Visitor Center (evening tour)
tips: Giulia recommends the evening guided visit. Book ahead on noa.gr.
places.background: The historic 1842 observatory on the Hill of the Nymphs runs evening visits with the Geoastrophysics museum, the historic Synge/Doridis telescopes and stargazing (weather permitting).
places.address: Hill of the Nymphs (Lofos Nymfon), Thissio, Athens 118 51

Photo: Dimboukas at English Wikipedia · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

places.name: Krabo
places.background: A seasonal beach restaurant and bar in the small Zoska cove at Kavouri, with paid sunbeds and cabanas. Lunch under a pergola is Mediterranean seafood, pasta and meze with Greek wines, followed by sunset cocktails.
places.address: Thespidos St, Zoska Bay, Kavouri, Vouliagmeni 166 71

places.name: Island (Island Club & Restaurant / Island Athens Riviera)
places.background: An upscale seaside summer restaurant and nightclub on the rocks at Varkiza: sunset dinner, then DJs and partying until early morning, with table and bottle service. It is long-running, with whitewashed Cycladic styling and sea views, a glamorous summer night out on the Riviera.
